identity.life_stage: single, line cook, plays bass in a bar band

engagement.interaction_backstory: He grew up in the church playing bass every Sunday from eleven years old and has not been in eight years. He came to the site as a musician, not a believer — he wanted to hear how the low end was mixed — and stayed longer than he intended. He has told nobody he still listens.

depth.core_contradiction: Left over the hypocrisy and has never once played in a band that did not sound like church.
depth.wound: He was the church's musician, never its member, and he figured that out at nineteen.
depth.longing: To be wanted somewhere for something other than what he can play.
depth.faith_journey: Raised in a Black Baptist church, gifted and used, walked out at eighteen without a scene; not angry, just done being furniture.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Understated; deflects with music talk; says "it's cool" to end conversations.
depth.open_doubt: Whether the thing he felt on that stage at fourteen was God or just volume.

social_graph.note: still in that church; still asks; he still says maybe
four guys who do not know he can read music

depth.emotional_weather_default: Easy and low; melancholy on Sunday mornings, which he finds funny.
depth.daily_texture: Kitchen until midnight, load-in Thursdays, the amp in the back seat, headphones on the walk home.
depth.sensory_anchor: A Sunday morning organ pedal coming in under him at fourteen.
depth.living_arc: One invitation away from playing in a church again, and it would have to be the right one.
